A2-R1.label: A2-R1  HAR design + Z1 RETURN outcome

A2-R2.label: A2-R2  ACTUAL Z1 design + Z1 return outcome

conclusion.headline: A2-R2 - the ACTUAL V3-Z1 design and outcome - rejects a true null 5.40% of the time at a nominal 5%. With 1,000 permutations the Monte-Carlo SE is 0.0069, so 5.40% sits within one SE of nominal. The V3-Z1 p-values are correctly calibrated.
conclusion.v2_v3_pvalues: VALIDATED for the return-outcome configuration actually used. The V2_PROXY and V3-Z1 negative conclusions rest on correctly sized tests.
conclusion.my_hypothesis_was_wrong: I attributed the A2 failure to heavy tails in log(r^2). The measurement refutes that: log(r^2) has kurtosis 3.59 (close to the normal value of 3) while the RETURN outcome has kurtosis 15.61 and larger skew. The return is the far heavier-tailed of the two, yet it is the one that produces correct size. Tails are not the mechanism.
conclusion.alternative_conjecture: UNTESTED. log(r^2) carries strong intraday seasonality - variance at the cash open is systematically higher than overnight - and so do the HAR predictors. The block permutation preserves hour-of-session alignment, so permuted X and Y still share that seasonal component. Six coarse session buckets may not absorb all of it, leaving a real shared signal under a nominal null. If so the 17.1% is an artifact of MY A2 design, not of CR1 and not of log(r^2). This is a conjecture; it has not been tested and should not be reported as the cause.
conclusion.what_is_settled: the CR1 implementation is not defective
